stories.headline: Yemen's Houthis strike Saudi energy facilities as US hits Iranian oil tankers
stories.body:
Yemen's Houthis launched drone and missile attacks against four southern Saudi cities on Tuesday. The strikes set oil installations on fire. They also wounded dozens of people. Saudi authorities said 73 people were hurt across southern Saudi Arabia. Women and children were among those injured. Fighting between government forces and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen is raising fears of full-scale war.

United States forces struck multiple Iranian oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. US officials said the strikes followed Iranian attempts to hit a US Navy warship. US officials told CNN that strikes targeted tankers near Kharg Island on Tuesday. Iranian state media said a US missile hit an Iranian tanker 6km from Kharg Island. State media said another tanker was attacked near Jask on the Gulf of Oman.

Iranian Armed Forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi issued a warning. Abdollahi said any attack on Iranian tankers would trigger strikes against US bases. He said these strikes would hit US bases across the region. The Revolutionary Guard warned crews on oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to leave immediately. The Guard threatened to target those vessels. International benchmark Brent crude briefly reached $99.46 a barrel on Tuesday as tensions in the Gulf rose.

The United States government announced new aviation sanctions against Iran. The Trump administration put sanctions on 27 Iranian airlines. It also targeted nine service providers accused of supporting Mahan Air. The Treasury designed these rules to ground Iranian airlines.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it captured a US submersible near the Strait of Hormuz. A US official said a defective underwater military drone had malfunctioned. US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins said an older-model surveillance drone submersible malfunctioned in regional waters. Hawkins said it contained no sensitive data. He said it had no classified radar equipment. The Revolutionary Guard also claimed it destroyed an MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz. It said it used a new Iranian air defence system.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said talks with Oman reached significant progress. He said the talks focused on managing the Strait of Hormuz. The broader conflict has claimed the lives of 18 US service members. Related violence occurred elsewhere in the region. Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed 13 people on Monday. The Lebanese Health Ministry reported that death toll.

claims.text: Yemen's Houthis launched drone and missile attacks against four southern Saudi cities on Tuesday, September 8, setting oil installations on fire and wounding dozens.
Saudi authorities reported that 73 people, including women and children, were hurt in the Houthi attacks across southern Saudi Arabia.
Fighting between government forces and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen is raising fears of a return to full-scale war.
US forces struck multiple Iranian tankers linked to the IRGC after Iranian attempts to hit a US Navy warship.
US officials told CNN that US strikes targeted multiple Iranian oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps near Kharg Island on Tuesday.
Iranian state media reported that a US missile struck an Iranian oil tanker 6km from Kharg Island and attacked another near Jask on the Gulf of Oman.
Iranian Armed Forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi warned that any attack on Iranian oil tankers would trigger strikes against US bases across the region.
The IRGC warned crews aboard oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to evacuate immediately, threatening to target the vessels.
International benchmark Brent crude briefly reached $99.46 a barrel on Tuesday amid rising Gulf tensions.
The US Treasury announced new aviation-related sanctions aimed at grounding Iranian airlines.
The Trump administration imposed sanctions targeting 27 Iranian airlines and nine service providers accused of supporting Mahan Air.
Iran's IRGC stated it captured a US submersible near the Strait of Hormuz, while a US official said a defective underwater military drone had malfunctioned.
US Navy Capt Tim Hawkins stated that a defective older-model US drone surveillance submersible malfunctioned in regional waters and contained no sensitive data or classified radar equipment.
The IRGC claimed it intercepted and destroyed an MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz using a new Iranian air defence system.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that talks with Oman on managing the Strait of Hormuz had achieved significant progress.
The conflict has claimed the lives of 18 US service members.
Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon on Monday killed 13 people, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry.

stories.headline: Britain, France, and Canada ban imports from West Bank settlements
stories.body:
Britain, France, and Canada announced trade restrictions blocking imports from Israeli West Bank settlements. Twelve countries acted together or considered measures against trade with settlements in the West Bank. The UK government banned goods from Israeli settlements there. It restricted services to settlements. It also put limits on arms sales that contribute to the occupation. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said settler terrorism in parts of the West Bank amounted to ethnic cleansing. He said the Israeli government turned a blind eye. Palestinian ambassador Dr Husam Zomlot called the trade decision a turning point. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said targeted measures were brought forward to support a two-state solution. Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch criticized the decision and accused the Labour government of antisemitism.

France cited the expansion of settlements and violence as its reason for banning goods. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said illegal settlements undermine long-term peace objectives. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington will not follow these bans.

Israel ordered the closure of the UK consulate in East Jerusalem. Israel also removed British representatives from the International Gaza Support Centre. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced entry bans on 12 Britons. Israel announced plans for 1,000 new West Bank homes on Tuesday.

claims.text: Britain, France, and Canada announced trade restrictions blocking imports from Israeli West Bank settlements.
Twelve countries, including Britain, France, Spain, and Canada, acted together in introducing or considering measures against trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
The UK government banned goods from Israeli West Bank settlements, restricted services to settlements, and placed limits on arms sales that contribute to the occupation.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated that settler terrorism in parts of the West Bank amounted to ethnic cleansing of Palestinians while the Israeli government turned a blind eye.
Palestinian ambassador Dr Husam Zomlot called the British government's trade decision a turning point in the UK-Palestine relationship.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that targeted measures were brought forward not against the Israeli people, but in support of a two-state solution.
UK Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch criticized the British government's decision to ban settlement trade and accused the Labour government of antisemitism.
France cited the frenzied expansion of settlements and a flare-up of violence as its rationale for banning West Bank settlement goods.
Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand stated on X that illegal settlements in the West Bank significantly undermine long-term peace objectives.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated Washington will not follow Britain, France, and Canada in blocking imports from Israeli settlements.
Israel ordered the closure of the UK's consulate in East Jerusalem and removed British representatives from the International Gaza Support Centre.
Israel announced the shutdown of the UK Consulate in occupied East Jerusalem following Britain's ban on settlement goods.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced retaliatory measures against the UK, including entry bans on 12 Britons such as former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn and 10 MPs.
Israel announced plans for 1,000 new West Bank homes on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Canada places counter-tariffs on $20 billion of US goods
stories.body:
Canada put counter-tariffs on roughly 20 billion dollars of American goods on Tuesday. The Canadian tariffs range from 15% to 50%. They target nearly 28 billion Canadian dollars worth of goods. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said the trade shift away from the US will cost money. Carney said it is necessary to protect Canadian workers. He said Canada is the largest customer for US goods in 26 states.

The US maintains a 25% tariff on Canadian cars, steel, aluminium, and lumber. It put 50% tariffs in late August on Canadian dairy, alcohol, hockey sticks, and perfume. Canada lost about 41,000 jobs in August after trade talks collapsed. Donald Trump threatened to block Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier from selling in the US. Trump wants Bombardier to move manufacturing to the United States. Bombardier employs over 3,000 people in the US.

The Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor opened recently. US officials did not attend the opening event. US consumers faced record average new car prices over $52,000 in September.

claims.text: Canada's counter-tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% came into force on Tuesday, targeting nearly C$28 billion ($20 billion) worth of American goods.
Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on around $20 billion of US goods went into effect at midnight on Tuesday.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated in a video address that Canada's trade pivot away from the US will come at a cost but is necessary to protect Canadian workers.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted that Canada is the largest customer for US goods in 26 states.
The US maintains a 25% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks, steel, aluminium, and lumber, alongside 50% tariffs imposed in late August on Canadian dairy, alcohol, hockey sticks, and perfume.
Canada lost roughly 41,000 jobs in August following the collapse of trade negotiations and new US tariffs.
Donald Trump threatened to block Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier from selling in the US market unless it moves manufacturing to the United States.
Bombardier employs over 3,000 people in the US and works with roughly 2,800 American companies across 47 states.
The Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit, Michigan and Windsor, Ontario opened recently without US officials attending the event.
US consumers faced record average new car sales prices exceeding $52,000 in September.

vocab.meaning: taxes imposed by a country in response to taxes set by another nation
the business of making products in large numbers in factories

stories.headline: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin hold hour-long phone call on Ukraine
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump held an hour-long phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday. Trump said he wanted a swift end to the war in Ukraine. The call followed a weekend visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. The envoys met Putin in Moscow on Saturday for over three hours. They then traveled to Kyiv on Sunday.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the call as constructive and frank. Ushakov said Putin told Trump that Russia has no aggressive plans towards European states. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked Trump for sending the envoys. Zelenskyy said peace ideas presented by Kushner included a couple of very good ideas. But Zelenskyy said he did not see a quick end to the conflict. Zelenskyy expressed hope to meet Trump around September 20 at the UN General Assembly.

Russian strikes killed at least five civilians in Kyiv on Tuesday morning. Ukrainian attacks caused casualties in Bryansk, Kursk, and Crimea. The European Commission approved a 3.7 billion dollar loan for Kyiv to buy Patriot parts.

claims.text: US President Donald Trump held an hour-long phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday, stating he wanted a swift end to the war in Ukraine.
The Putin-Trump call followed a weekend visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday for over three hours before traveling to Kyiv on Sunday.
Yuri Ushakov described the hour-long telephone call between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as constructive and quite frank.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov stated that Vladimir Putin told Donald Trump that Russia has no aggressive plans towards European states.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked Donald Trump for allowing US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to visit Ukraine despite ongoing fighting.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the peace ideas presented by US envoy Jared Kushner included a couple of very good, worthwhile ideas.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated following talks with US envoys that he did not see a quick end to the conflict.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed hope to meet Donald Trump around September 20 during the UN General Assembly in New York.
Russian strikes on Tuesday morning killed at least five civilians and wounded 25 others in Kyiv, while Ukrainian attacks caused casualties in Bryansk, Kursk, and Crimea.
The European Commission approved a 3.2 billion euro ($3.7 billion) loan for Kyiv to purchase components for Patriot air defence systems.

helpful and serving a useful purpose

stories.headline: Delhi authorities order building audits after seven die in housing collapse
stories.body:
Delhi authorities ordered building audits after seven people died in a five-storey house collapse on Sunday. The building housed a boys' paying guest accommodation in Satya Niketan. It was undergoing basement repairs and ground-floor renovation work when it collapsed. Delhi Police arrested property owner Urmila Gupta, her husband Hariram, and their son Mahesh. They face charges of culpable homicide and negligence. Police also apprehended labour contractor Sanoj in Uttar Pradesh.

The Municipal Corporation of Delhi demolished 24 properties across Delhi after the collapse. It also sealed seven illegal structures. The MCD suspended South Zone deputy commissioner Rakesh Kumar and four engineers. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta instructed officials to demolish an adjacent dilapidated building. Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu ordered a structural audit of all student housing hubs within a week.

A Supreme Court bench agreed to examine student housing collapses across India. The Delhi High Court directed the MCD to inspect all paying guest accommodations. It criticized authorities for failing to build enough hostels.

claims.text: A five-storey building housing a boys' paying guest accommodation in Satya Niketan collapsed on Sunday afternoon, killing seven people and injuring several others.
Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu ordered a structural audit of all buildings in paying guest accommodation hubs within a week.
The Satya Niketan building was undergoing basement repairs and ground-floor commercial extension renovation work when it collapsed.
Delhi Police arrested property owner Urmila Gupta, her husband Hariram Gupta, and their son Mahesh Gupta on charges of culpable homicide and negligence following the building collapse.
Labour contractor Sanoj was apprehended by police in Kasganj, Uttar Pradesh, for questioning in connection with the Satya Niketan collapse.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi demolished 24 properties and sealed seven illegal structures across Delhi following the Satya Niketan collapse.
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi suspended South Zone deputy commissioner Rakesh Kumar and four engineers pending disciplinary proceedings.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta instructed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi to demolish a dilapidated building adjacent to the collapse site in Satya Niketan.
A Supreme Court bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan agreed to examine PG building collapses and safety concerns across India.
A Delhi High Court bench comprising Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia directed the MCD to inspect all paying guest accommodations and submit a compliance report within a week.
The Delhi High Court criticized Delhi University and municipal authorities for failing to provide adequate hostel facilities, forcing students into unsafe paying guest accommodations.

stories.headline: Prime Minister Modi calls for global expansion of UPI at Fintech Fest
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the seventh edition of the Global Fintech Fest. During his speech, Modi urged the fintech ecosystem to expand the global reach of UPI. UPI is a real-time payment system developed in India. Real-time payment transactions using UPI reached 24.51 billion as of August.

The UPI platform is expanding across international borders. It is currently live in 11 countries. In addition, the platform is linked directly with Singapore's local payment system. Modi asked financial technology companies to take the system into even more nations.

Modi also urged the fintech industry to look beyond payments. He asked firms to focus heavily on non-payment transactions. Specifically, he called for wider access to savings products. He urged companies to expand access to pensions. He also encouraged them to provide better access to insurance.

Modi spoke about the strength of the national economy. He said India's economy achieved 7.8 per cent real GDP growth in the June quarter. He stressed that the country hit this growth rate despite challenges. Those economic challenges came from the ongoing conflict in West Asia.

Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra also addressed the Global Fintech Fest. Malhotra said Indian fintech firms have reshaped finance. He said these companies succeeded by taking banking directly into the hands of every citizen.

The country received positive news regarding its economic rating. Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India's sovereign credit rating. It raised the rating to 'A-' from 'BBB+'. This move was the agency's first upgrade for India in three decades.

claims.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the seventh edition of the Global Fintech Fest and urged the fintech ecosystem to expand UPI's global reach.
Real-time payment transactions using UPI reached 24.51 billion as of August.
The UPI platform is currently live in 11 countries and is linked with Singapore's local payment system.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged the fintech industry to focus on non-payment transactions, including access to savings products, pensions, and insurance.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that India's economy achieved 7.8 per cent real GDP growth in the June quarter despite challenges from the West Asia conflict.
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated at the Global Fintech Fest that Indian fintech firms have reshaped finance by taking banking directly into the hands of every citizen.
Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India's sovereign credit rating to 'A-' from 'BBB+', its first such upgrade for India in three decades.
